findings.title: Multiple full crypto providers no longer fail closed
findings.body: detectProvider now sorts by CryptoProvider.order() and silently keeps the first entry, logging the rest as ignored. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same order (200), so a classpath that contains more than one of them no longer throws. ServiceLoader encounter order then decides which implementation is used. A FIPS deployment that accidentally also sees the non-FIPS provider can run non-FIPS crypto with no error, which is the failure mode the previous "multiple providers" check existed to prevent. FIPS needs a strictly higher order than the non-FIPS providers, and equal top orders should still be treated as a hard error.

findings.title: AuthzClient.create locks in the global CryptoProvider
findings.body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) calls CryptoIntegration.init with AuthzClient's classloader. CryptoIntegration.init is process-wide and a no-op once cryptoProvider is set, so the first caller wins forever. ServiceLoader only sees META-INF/services resources of the classloader it is given. If that loader does not delegate to the server/test loader that contains DefaultCryptoProvider or FIPS1402Provider (typical with Keycloak's modular classloaders), the only hit is AuthzClientCryptoProvider. That stub then becomes the JVM-wide provider even if the server later initializes with the correct classloader. Almost every method on AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException, and getBouncyCastleProvider returns the platform KeyStore provider rather than BouncyCastle, so subsequent PEM, signature, and JWE operations fail or run against the wrong JCA provider.

findings.title: ES384/ES512 tests use a default P-256 key
findings.body: The suite generates one KeyPair via KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() with no ECGenParameterSpec and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. The JDK default curve is P-256, whose coordinates are 32 bytes, while ES384 and ES512 require 48-byte and 66-byte R/S values and matching curves (secp384r1, secp521r1). initSign can throw InvalidKeyException on those algorithms, or the conversion is only exercised for 32-byte integers padded out to the longer signature length. Either way the test does not prove concatenatedRSToASN1DER / asn1derToConcatenatedRS for the sizes those algorithms actually produce.
